newsitem.title: USA: US cigarette sales rose in 94, ad spending off - FTC.
newsitem.headline: US cigarette sales rose in 94, ad spending off - FTC.

text.p: Sales of cigarettes by major domestic manufacturers in the United States rose 6.2 percent in 1994 to 490.2 billion, the first increase in 10 years, the U.S. Federal Trade Commission said Wednesday.
Its latest annual report to Congress on cigarette sales and advertising said sales fell 8.9 percent in 1993.
The FTC said a large part of the rise in sales in 1994, the latest year for which data have been compiled, is due to changes in inventories rather than actual consumption.
The industry spent $4.83 billion on advertising and promotions in 1994, 19.9 percent less than the $6.09 billion spent in 1993 and the first fall since 1986.
